sections.heading: Keep It Running. Tell You When It Can't.
body: Most companies push a new system at the first big repair. The quote shows up before anyone has found what failed, and a worn part turns into a whole new furnace.

We do it the other way around. We find out what failed, fix it if fixing makes sense, and keep your system running as long as it honestly can. When it can't, we say so and show you the repair and the replacement side by side.
The decision stays yours, and it's made with the facts in front of you.

sections.heading: What You Notice, and What We Do About It
body: Most breakdowns start with something small you can see or hear. Here's what we usually find behind it, and what we do.

items.title: The house won't get below 80
items.text: Dirty coils make a unit work harder for less cooling, and a refrigerant leak leaves it running without cooling at all. We run leak detection and fix the leak instead of just topping off the refrigerant.

items.title: The outdoor unit hums and never starts
items.text: A weak capacitor is a common cause, and it's a small part. We test it and replace the part, not the unit.

items.title: The furnace clicks but never lights
items.text: Often a worn ignitor or a wiring fault, and sometimes a filter so clogged the furnace can't breathe. We find which one it is and repair that.

items.title: The furnace lights, then shuts off
items.text: Airflow is the first thing to check, because a choked filter makes a furnace shut itself down. We check airflow and the burner side, then fix what we find.

items.title: One room is always too hot or too cold
items.text: A duct that leaks, is crushed or doesn't reach the room can leave a good unit looking like a bad one. We make fittings to your measurements in our own sheet metal shop.

items.title: The repair bills keep coming
items.text: On an old system, the repairs can start to cost more than they're worth. We put the repair next to a new system and show you both.

sections.heading: When a Repair Stops Making Sense
body: Here's a rule you can check yourself. A capacitor, an ignitor or a motor is a repair on a system that still has years in it. The age is on the label on the unit.
A failed compressor or a cracked heat exchanger on an old system, or repairs that keep stacking up, is when to price a new one. Ask any company to tell you in plain words what failed.
Told you need a whole new system? Call us for a second look before you spend that money.

sections.heading: Dry Air, Dust and Stuffy Rooms
body: A closed house carries dust, pet dander and whatever your filter misses, and the system moves it through every room several times an hour. In winter the heat dries the air out, and you get static shocks and cracked lips.
We install filters in a range of sizes. Whole-system filtration goes on any existing system and removes up to 90% of air contaminants, and a humidifier on the furnace puts the moisture back.

items.q: How do I know whether to repair or replace?
items.a: It depends on the age of the system and what failed. The age is on the label on the unit, and most furnaces and air conditioners give you well over ten years. One failed part on a system with years left is a repair. An old system with repairs piling up, or a failed compressor or heat exchanger, is worth pricing a replacement.

items.q: Another company says I need a whole new system. Should I get a second look?
items.a: Yes. Ask that company to write down what failed. If the answer is the whole system and not a part, call us and we'll look at it ourselves.

sections.heading: What Happens When You Call About a New System
body: You tell us what you have and what it's doing. We start from a diagnosis, not a new system, because a failed ignitor or a bad capacitor is a repair, not a replacement.
If the system is finished, we lay out the repair and the replacement side by side, and the decision is yours. Already been told you need a whole new system? Call us for a second look.

sections.heading: Repair or Replace
body: Here's a rule you can check yourself. Furnaces commonly run 15 to 20 years and air conditioners 10 to 15. If yours is near the end of that range and a single repair costs about half of what a new unit would, price the replacement.
If the unit is well inside that range and the problem is one part, repair it. We'll tell you which one you're looking at.

sections.heading: When the Old System Is Done
body: The signs arrive over a few seasons: repairs that come more often and cost more, a unit that runs nearly all day, one room that's always too hot or too cold, an energy bill that creeps up.
At some point you're paying to keep a system alive that you'd be better off replacing, and we'll say so when we see it.

sections.heading: Ducts Made to Fit Your House
body: A new unit only works as well as the ducts around it. A system that's too big turns on and off in short bursts and leaves the air clammy. One that's too small runs all day.
Leaky or crushed ductwork wastes what the new unit makes, and no unit can fix a room it can't reach.
That's why we have our own sheet metal shop. When a fitting or a duct run has to fit an odd space, we make it to your measurements instead of forcing a stock part close enough.

sections.heading: What a Servicing Looks For
body: Most furnace and air conditioner failures start as something small. A servicing is when someone checks for it, while the weather is mild and the part is still cheap.

items.title: A filter that's clogged or the wrong size
items.text: It makes the blower strain and chokes airflow. We check it and swap it for the right one.

items.title: Dirty coils on the air conditioner
items.text: They make the unit work harder for less cooling. We check them before the first hot week.

items.title: A loose wire or a tired connection
items.text: It holds on until the first hard freeze and then doesn't. We check the wiring and the connections.

items.title: A worn ignitor on the furnace
items.text: It's behind many a furnace that clicks and never lights. Caught early, it's a small repair.

items.title: A slow refrigerant leak
items.text: The unit still runs but cools less each summer. We run leak detection on air conditioners.

items.title: Carbon monoxide from a furnace that burns poorly
items.text: You can't smell it. If you burn gas for heat, we run carbon monoxide detection.
